A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rebus-puzzle study and provide readable text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices A–L. The retained material and additions can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations on 432 puzzles, including prompting experiments, iterative refinement, caption-only evaluation, and image retrieval.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-5 and Molmo evaluations, an alternative-judge experiment, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The puzzle-solving prompts, skill guidance, iterative refinement, caption generation, and retrieval procedures are unchanged. The added models are evaluated comparators; the second judge provides evaluation validation rather than a new proposed model or solving method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 432 English-language puzzles with the same 11 skill categories and retained input scenarios. The additional model evaluations and qualitative examples use this existing benchmark. Human-participant details are newly disclosed, without evidence of changed population coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5, Molmo-72B-0924, and Molmo-7B-D-0924 to the existing comparator roster. Table 2 adds GPT-5 and Molmo-72B-0924 to the per-skill comparison. Previously evaluated comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds a validation protocol using Qwen3-8B with thinking enabled to judge outputs from four models alongside GPT-4o. Existing scoring definitions and prompting protocols remain unchanged. The human-evaluation paragraph documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Table H.1 adds a check of sensitivity to judge choice. Figure K.2 adds three cases—blanket, mess around, and stay indoors—contrasting o4-mini successes with Claude-3.5-haiku or Phi-4 failures. Earlier prompting, refinement, and perception analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe the same bootstrap procedure and report 95% confidence intervals. New result rows reuse this reporting practice. No repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged, with additions in Tables 1, 2, and H.1 and Figure K.2. GPT-5 becomes the reported leader at 60.42% naive and 69.44% LLM-judged accuracy; v1's respective leaders were o3 at 54.56% and o4-mini at 55.62%. These are new model evaluations, not improved reruns. The alternative judge preserves the four evaluated models' ranking.

T1.justification: The retrieval-metric definitions in Appendix G and correctness and bootstrap-accuracy formulas in Appendix H are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about lateral-reasoning weaknesses, limited benefits from hints, and the gap from expert solvers. Additional model results do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly qualifies the human comparison as illustrative rather than rigorous. It also interprets the alternative judge's similar scores and unchanged ranking as evidence of consistent cross-model validation. Earlier mechanism explanations and the main limitations discussion are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly discloses one expert and four non-expert lab volunteers, their English-language backgrounds, and 25–200 randomly selected puzzles per participant; the human scores already appeared in v1. The first page also adds project-page and direct dataset links. Existing code licensing and decoding disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds a short discussion of Bongard in Wonderland with a Dai et al. (2024) citation and reference entry. The substantive comparisons with REBUS and COLUMBUS, including Appendix B, and the claimed research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief background and evaluation paragraphs and makes small updates to the results summary and qualitative-example references. The main section sequence, narrative, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 gain rows, and Table H.1 and Figure K.2 are added. Existing displays, including Table 4 and Figure K.1, are relocated as the document reflows. First-page resource links are added; the original figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by documenting the previously unexplained human evaluation and its limited purpose. The second-judge check provides useful evidence that four models' rankings are stable, while added model results and examples extend the empirical picture. These gains are limited: judge validation covers only four models, and the human comparison remains illustrative.
